epithet.en: Athenian philosopher on trial for his life

1.modern-en: Socrates opens his defense before the Athenian jury, refusing polished rhetoric in favor of plain truth. He recounts how the Oracle at Delphi called him wisest, and how his lifetime of questioning men who claimed wisdom—politicians, poets, craftsmen—earned him powerful enemies. He denies being a Sophist or a teacher for pay.
1.modern-da: Sokrates åbner sit forsvar over for den athenske jury og afviser poleret retorik til fordel for simpel sandhed. Han fortæller, hvordan oraklet i Delphi kaldte ham den klogeste, og hvordan hans livslange udspørgning af folk, der hævdede at have visdom, skaffede ham mægtige fjender. Han benægter at være sofist eller betalt lærer.

2.modern-en: Convicted by a narrow majority, Socrates refuses to propose exile or silence as a penalty. He argues he has been the city's greatest benefactor and suggests he deserves free meals at the Prytaneum. At the urging of friends he offers thirty minas as a fine.
2.modern-da: Dømt med et lille flertal nægter Sokrates at foreslå eksil eller tavshed som straf. Han hævder, at han har været byens største velgører, og antyder, at han fortjener gratis måltider i Prytaneum. På opfordring fra venner tilbyder han tredive miner som bøde.

3.modern-en: Sentenced to death, Socrates addresses his judges with equanimity. He prophesies that questioners will multiply after his death, reflects on why his divine sign never opposed him today, and argues that death is either dreamless sleep or a journey to the just. He leaves the court at peace.
3.modern-da: Dømt til døden taler Sokrates til sine dommere med sindsro. Han profeterer, at udspørgere vil mangfoldiggøres efter hans død, overvejer hvorfor hans guddommelige tegn aldrig modsatte sig ham i dag, og hævder, at døden enten er drømmefri søvn eller en rejse til de retfærdige. Han forlader retten i fred.

epithet.en: Poet and chief accuser of Socrates

1.modern-en: Meletus is the formal accuser who charges Socrates with impiety and corrupting the youth. Socrates cross-examines him in open court, exposing the contradiction that Meletus claims all Athenians improve the young—except Socrates—and that Socrates simultaneously believes in no gods and in new divine beings.
1.modern-da: Meletos er den formelle anklager, der sigter Sokrates for ugudelighed og ungdomsfordærvelse. Sokrates afhører ham i retten og afslører modsigelsen om, at Meletos hævder, at alle athenere opdrager de unge godt – undtagen Sokrates – og at Sokrates på én gang er ateist og tilhænger af nye guddommelige væsener.

2.modern-en: Meletus proposed the death penalty. Socrates notes that without the support of Anytus and Lycon, Meletus would not have received a fifth of the votes required to avoid a fine—meaning his prosecution was effectively a failure by legal standards.
2.modern-da: Meletos foreslog dødsstraf. Sokrates bemærker, at uden støtte fra Anytos og Lykon ville Meletos ikke have modtaget en femtedel af de nødvendige stemmer og dermed selv have stået til en bøde — hans tiltale var altså reelt en fiasko efter lovens målestok.

1.modern-en: Anytus is cited as a powerful co-accuser acting on behalf of craftsmen and politicians. Socrates describes him as the more dangerous political force behind the prosecution, though he does not speak or appear directly in the dialogue.
1.modern-da: Anytos nævnes som en magtfuld medsagsøger, der handler på vegne af håndværkere og politikere. Sokrates beskriver ham som den farligste politiske kraft bag anklagen, selvom han ikke optræder direkte i dialogen.

2.modern-en: Socrates mentions Anytus again in noting that Meletus's charge needed the backing of Anytus and Lycon to reach the required vote threshold—evidence of how politically orchestrated the prosecution was.
2.modern-da: Sokrates nævner igen Anytos, da han påpeger, at Meletos' anklage krævede opbakning fra Anytos og Lykon for at nå den nødvendige stemmegrænse — et tegn på, hvor politisk tilrettelagt tiltalen var.

1.modern-en: Lycon is briefly mentioned as the third co-accuser alongside Meletus and Anytus, acting on behalf of the orators. He has no speaking role.
1.modern-da: Lykon nævnes kort som den tredje medsagsøger ved siden af Meletos og Anytos, der handler på vegne af talerne. Han har ingen talerolle.

2.modern-en: Lycon is mentioned again as one of the backers whose support helped Meletus's prosecution meet its legal vote threshold.
2.modern-da: Lykon nævnes igen som en af de støtter, hvis opbakning hjalp Meletos' tiltale med at nå den lovpligtige stemmegrænse.

epithet.en: Devoted friend who consulted the Oracle

1.modern-en: Chaerephon is invoked by Socrates as a key witness: it was he who asked the Oracle at Delphi whether anyone was wiser than Socrates, and received the famous reply that no one was. Though dead by the time of the trial, his brother is present to confirm the story.
1.modern-da: Chairefon fremhæves af Sokrates som et vigtigt vidne: det var ham, der spurgte oraklet i Delphi, om nogen var klogere end Sokrates, og fik det berømte svar, at ingen var det. Selvom han er død ved tidspunktet for retssagen, er hans bror til stede for at bekræfte historien.
